title: Hierarchical Page Permissions
prompt:
Implement `PagePermissions` for a tree of pages. Roles are ordered `none < view < comment < edit`. Provide `add_page(page, parent=None)`, `add_user_to_group(user, group)`, `grant_user(page, user, role)`, `grant_group(page, group, role)`, `getUserPermissionForPage(page, user)`, and `getAllUsersWithPermissionForPage(page, min_role='view')`.

A user's effective permission is the strongest applicable direct-user or direct-group grant on the requested page or any ancestor. `getUserPermissionForPage` returns a role string. `getAllUsersWithPermissionForPage` returns sorted user IDs whose effective role meets `min_role`; users with no applicable grant are excluded. Page IDs, user IDs, and group IDs are nonempty strings; unknown pages and invalid values raise `ValueError`. `add_page` may only name an existing parent, so the structure remains a tree.

This is a practice reconstruction because the report did not publish precise revocation semantics; this version models grants as monotonic along the ancestor chain.

example.reasoning: The root grant is inherited by the child page.
